compare-contractor-quotes-uae.title: How to compare contractor quotes in the UAE without getting burned
compare-contractor-quotes-uae.excerpt: Three quotes that look similar can hide very different scopes. Here is how UAE buyers read past the bottom line.
compare-contractor-quotes-uae.meta_desc: A practical guide to comparing contractor and supplier quotes in the UAE — scope, exclusions, payment terms, approvals and the traps that make the cheapest quote the most expensive.
compare-contractor-quotes-uae.body_html:
The cheapest quote is rarely the cheapest project. In the UAE, where the same job can be priced by a one-man trade licence or a fully-staffed contractor, the number at the bottom of the page tells you almost nothing on its own. Here is how experienced buyers actually compare.

1. Compare scope before price

Line up every quote against the same checklist: what materials, what brand or grade, what quantity, and crucially what is excluded. A quote that excludes authority approvals, MEP works, making-good, or site cleaning can look 15% cheaper and end up more expensive once those gaps are filled by variation orders.

2. Read the exclusions, not just the inclusions

UAE quotations often bury the real story in an "exclusions" or "clarifications" section. Common ones to watch: VAT not included, Dubai Municipality / DDA / Civil Defence approval fees by client, removal of existing works, and warranty limited to "manufacturing defects only".

3. Check the specification, not the adjective

"High quality" means nothing. A railing quoted with 5mm glass is not comparable to one with 6mm tempered glass; "powder coated" is not the same as marine-grade powder coat. Ask every supplier to state the exact grade, thickness, standard (e.g. UL/FM, NFPA, ISO) and brand.

4. Weigh delivery against your real deadline

A four-week lead time is worth paying for if your handover is fixed; it is worth nothing if you have three months. Don't pay a premium for speed you don't need — but do confirm whether the timeline is from order, from advance payment, or from approval.

5. Understand the payment terms

Advance percentage, milestone payments, and retention all change the real cost of money. A 50% advance to a supplier you don't know is a different risk than 20% on delivery. In the UAE, retention of 5–10% held until the defects-liability period ends is normal for larger works.

6. Separate the price from the relationship

Track record matters: ask for two recent reference projects of similar size, and check the trade licence covers the activity you're buying. A supplier licensed for "general maintenance" quoting a full fit-out is a red flag.

fit-out-quote-dubai-checklist.title: What a fair office fit-out quote in Dubai should include
fit-out-quote-dubai-checklist.excerpt: A proper fit-out quote is more than flooring and paint. Use this checklist before you sign anything.
fit-out-quote-dubai-checklist.meta_desc: A checklist of what a complete office fit-out quotation in Dubai should cover — approvals, MEP, joinery, HVAC, fire compliance, defects liability — so you can spot underscoped quotes.
fit-out-quote-dubai-checklist.body_html:
Office fit-out is where underscoped quotes do the most damage, because so much of the cost is invisible until the work starts. A complete Dubai fit-out quotation should address all of the following — if any are missing, ask why.

Authority approvals

Fit-out works in Dubai typically need landlord NOC and approval from the relevant authority — Dubai Municipality, DDA, Trakhees, DMCC or the free-zone authority depending on location, plus Civil Defence for anything touching fire or life-safety systems. Confirm whether approval drawings, fees and follow-up are in the contractor's scope or yours.

MEP works

Mechanical, electrical and plumbing is the single most common exclusion. Lighting, power points, data, HVAC modifications, drainage for a pantry or washroom — these should be itemised, not assumed.

HVAC and the chilled-water / FAHU interface

Re-balancing the AC after partitions change the airflow is real work. A quote that adds partitions but ignores HVAC re-balancing will leave you with hot and cold zones.

Fire and life safety

New partitions usually mean relocating smoke detectors, sprinkler heads and emergency lighting, plus Civil Defence sign-off. This must be in the quote and the programme.

Joinery and finishes

Specify materials precisely: laminate grade, ironmongery brand, paint type and number of coats, flooring type and skirting. "As per design" is not a specification.

Making good, cleaning and handover

Removal of existing works, protection of common areas, post-construction cleaning, and as-built drawings are legitimate costs. So is a snagging period.

Defects-liability period

A serious contractor offers a defects-liability period (commonly 12 months) and states retention terms. No warranty at all is a warning sign.

Programme and payment

A week-by-week programme tied to milestone payments protects both sides. Match the payment schedule to delivered milestones, not to the calendar.

fire-fighting-systems-uae-civil-defence.title: Fire-fighting systems in the UAE: approvals, standards and what to ask suppliers
fire-fighting-systems-uae-civil-defence.excerpt: Civil Defence approval, NFPA standards and UL/FM listings decide whether your fire system passes. Here is what to specify.
fire-fighting-systems-uae-civil-defence.meta_desc: A buyer guide to procuring fire-fighting systems in the UAE — Civil Defence approval, NFPA 20/13 standards, UL/FM listed equipment, and the questions to ask every supplier.
fire-fighting-systems-uae-civil-defence.body_html:
Fire-fighting is one area where the cheapest quote can literally fail inspection. UAE projects are governed by the UAE Fire and Life Safety Code of Practice, enforced by Civil Defence, and the requirements are specific. Here's what to specify and ask.

Civil Defence approval is non-negotiable

Fire systems must be designed, installed and commissioned by Civil-Defence-approved contractors, with approved drawings and a final inspection before occupancy. Always confirm the supplier is an approved contractor and that approval drawings and sign-off are in scope.

Know the standards that apply

  • NFPA 20 — installation of stationary fire pumps.
  • NFPA 13 — sprinkler system design.
  • NFPA 14 — standpipe and hose systems.
  • NFPA 72 — fire alarm and detection.

A quote should state which standards it is built to, not just "as per Civil Defence".

Insist on UL/FM listed equipment

Pumps, valves and key components should be UL listed and/or FM approved. "UL listed, FM pending" is not the same as FM approved — and that gap can stall your inspection. Make the listing an explicit line item.

Match the duty to the building

Pump flow (GPM) and pressure (bar), tank capacity, and standby/jockey pump arrangement must match the building's hydraulic calculation — not a generic figure. Ask for the basis of the sizing.

Commissioning, AMC and spares

Commissioning, witnessed testing, and a maintenance contract (AMC) keep the system compliant after handover. A quote that includes commissioning and a defined warranty is worth more than a bare supply price.

Ask the right routing question

A fire-pump enquiry should go to fire-fighting specialists — not a general MEP or steel-pipe supplier. On QuotesDone, the matching engine routes by actual capability, so a pump enquiry reaches genuine fire-fighting suppliers and never lands as spam in an unrelated trade's inbox.

What a proper service includes

  • Repeated gas refills instead of finding and fixing the leak
  • No written parts warranty on repairs
  • Prices quoted before anyone has seen the system

FAQs

How often should AC be serviced in the UAE?
Given the climate, most homes service every 3–6 months; an annual contract usually covers 2–4 visits with at least one chemical clean.
Why is a gas refill expensive?
It depends on the refrigerant type and amount. A recurring refill usually signals a leak that should be repaired rather than topped up again and again.
Is an annual AC contract worth it?
For two or more units it is usually cheaper than ad-hoc call-outs and includes scheduled cleaning that lowers bills and breakdowns.
What is a fair price to install a new split AC?
Supply and install of a 1–2 ton split typically runs AED 1,800–4,500 depending on brand, bracket work and pipe run — compare at least two quotes.

How many coats should I expect?
Two coats over primer is standard. One coat is a common way cheap quotes cut corners — it rarely covers evenly.
Do I need to move out during painting?
No — most jobs are done room by room; just clear or cover furniture.

An annual maintenance contract (AMC) keeps your air conditioning running efficiently, cuts the risk of a mid-summer breakdown, and spreads the cost across the year. But AMC pricing in the UAE varies wildly depending on unit type, number of units, and what the contract actually includes. Here is a practical 2026 breakdown for SMEs, retail units, offices and villas.

Typical AC maintenance contract prices in the UAE (2026)

AMCs are usually priced per unit per year, with a set number of scheduled visits. As a working guide:

  • Split / wall-mounted unit: AED 250-500 per unit per year (typically 2-4 visits).
  • Cassette / ceiling unit: AED 350-650 per unit per year.
  • Ducted / concealed split: AED 500-900 per unit per year (more filters and duct access).
  • Package / rooftop unit: AED 900-2,000 per unit per year.
  • Central / chilled water (FCU + AHU): priced per system, often AED 3,000-15,000+ per year depending on tonnage and building size.

Small offices and villas with 3-6 split units commonly land between AED 1,200 and AED 3,000 per year for a comprehensive contract. Retail and F&B units with heavier loads pay more because units run longer hours.

Comprehensive vs non-comprehensive contracts

This is the single biggest reason two quotes differ by hundreds of dirhams:

  • Non-comprehensive (labour only): covers scheduled servicing and callouts, but you pay for spare parts, gas top-ups and compressors separately. Cheaper upfront.
  • Comprehensive: includes most parts, refrigerant top-ups and some repairs. Higher price, fewer surprise bills. Read exclusions carefully, compressors are often still excluded.

What a good AC maintenance contract should include

Before you compare prices, agree on scope. A solid AMC should cover:

  • Scheduled preventive visits (state how many per year and roughly when).
  • Filter cleaning or replacement at each visit.
  • Coil cleaning, drain line clearing and gas pressure checks.
  • Electrical connection and thermostat checks.
  • Emergency callout response time (e.g. within 24-48 hours).
  • A service report after each visit.

Note what is not included: compressor replacement, major duct cleaning, and gas refills beyond a top-up are common exclusions.

What drives your AMC price up or down

  • Number of units: more units usually means a lower per-unit rate.
  • Unit type and age: older or ducted systems need more labour and parts.
  • Operating hours: a restaurant or clinic running 16 hours a day wears units faster than a 9-to-5 office.
  • Visit frequency: 4 visits a year costs more than 2, but is worth it in the Gulf climate.
  • Response guarantees: faster emergency response and after-hours cover add a premium.

How to compare AC maintenance quotes fairly

Cheap AMCs often hide their value in the exclusions. To compare like for like:

  • List every unit by type and location so all suppliers quote the same scope.
  • Ask for price per unit per year, not just a lump sum.
  • Confirm the number of visits and whether callouts are included or charged.
  • Ask what parts are covered and get exclusions in writing.
  • Check the response time commitment and whether it is genuinely guaranteed.

Two to four is standard. Homes and light-use offices manage on two, while retail, clinics and F&B with heavy usage benefit from three or four to keep coils clean and efficiency high during peak summer.

Is a comprehensive AMC worth the extra cost?

Reconfiguring an office in Dubai, Abu Dhabi or Sharjah almost always comes down to one question: how do we split the space? Partitions are the fastest way to create meeting rooms, private offices and quiet zones without a full fit-out. This 2026 guide breaks down realistic UAE partition prices, what moves the cost, and how to compare quotes without getting caught out.

Typical office partition costs in the UAE (2026)

Prices are usually quoted per square metre of partition wall (height x length), supplied and installed. As a working reference for the UAE market in 2026:

  • Gypsum (drywall) partitions: roughly AED 90–180 per sqm for a standard single-stud, double-boarded wall. Add insulation and acoustic board and you move toward the top of that range.
  • Aluminium-framed glass partitions: roughly AED 350–650 per sqm depending on glass thickness, frame profile and finish.
  • Frameless / structural glass partitions: roughly AED 600–1,100 per sqm, higher for double-glazed acoustic glass.
  • Demountable / modular systems (imported): roughly AED 900–2,000+ per sqm — premium because panels are reusable and relocatable.

Doors, blinds, film, and any electrical or ELV routing inside the partition are usually priced separately, so always check whether they are included.

Which type suits which need?

  • Gypsum — best value for solid private offices and stores where you do not need light or a view through.
  • Glass — the choice for a modern, open feel; good for meeting rooms and manager cabins that still need light.
  • Demountable — worth it if your business relocates or reconfigures often, since the panels can be dismantled and reused.

What actually drives the price

Two quotes for the same room can differ widely, and it is rarely just markup. The main cost drivers are:

  • Glass specification: 10mm vs 12mm, single vs double glazing, and acoustic laminated glass all change the number significantly.
  • Acoustic rating: proper sound insulation (insulation infill, sealed head/base tracks, acoustic seals on glass) adds material and labour.
  • Height: partitions running to a high slab or above a false ceiling cost more than those stopping at ceiling level.
  • Doors and hardware: hinged, sliding or frameless glass doors with floor springs and closers can add several thousand dirhams each.
  • Finishes: paint-ready gypsum vs skimmed and painted, powder-coated frame colours, and manifestation film all add up.
  • Site conditions and access: occupied offices, after-hours work, and buildings requiring fit-out permits and NOCs push labour costs higher.

Don't forget permits and building rules

Most UAE commercial towers and free zones require approval before you alter the layout. That can mean a fit-out permit, landlord NOC, and compliance with civil defence rules for fire exits and sprinkler coverage. A partition that blocks an emergency route or a sprinkler head will be rejected. A good contractor prices this in and handles the drawings; a cheap quote that ignores it can cost you more later.

How to compare partition quotes fairly

To compare like for like, make sure every quote states:

  • Partition type and exact glass thickness / gypsum build-up
  • Total square metres and linear metres
  • Acoustic rating (if any)
  • Doors, hardware and film — included or excluded
  • Permits, NOCs and civil defence approval responsibility
  • Making good, painting and cleanup
  • Warranty and expected timeline

  • Use gypsum where privacy matters more than light, and reserve glass for feature rooms.

A single meeting room can be installed in one to two days. A full floor reconfiguration with glass and doors typically runs one to three weeks, plus lead time for imported glass or demountable systems and any permit approvals.

Are glass partitions worth the extra cost over gypsum?

If natural light, an open feel and a modern look matter, glass is usually worth it. For pure privacy or storage rooms where a view through adds nothing, gypsum delivers the same function for a fraction of the price.

Do I need civil defence approval for office partitions?

Often yes. Any change that affects fire exits, escape routes or sprinkler coverage generally requires fit-out permit and civil defence sign-off in UAE commercial buildings. Confirm who is responsible for approvals before signing.

how-much-does-cctv-installation-cost-in-.body_html:
CCTV is one of the most common security upgrades UAE businesses ask about, yet quotes vary wildly. One supplier says AED 1,500, another says AED 6,000 for what looks like the same job. This 2026 guide explains what actually drives CCTV installation cost in the UAE, so you can budget accurately and compare like-for-like.

Typical CCTV installation costs in the UAE (2026)

Pricing depends on camera type, resolution, number of cameras, cabling distance, and whether you need a SIRA-compliant setup. As indicative ranges for a supply-and-install job:

  • Per camera (2MP HD analog): AED 250 - AED 600 installed
  • Per camera (4MP-8MP IP): AED 600 - AED 1,500 installed
  • 4-camera package (basic HD): AED 1,200 - AED 2,500
  • 8-camera package (IP, NVR, remote view): AED 3,500 - AED 7,500
  • 16-camera commercial system: AED 8,000 - AED 20,000+

These are guidance figures only. Actual quotes shift with brand, site conditions and compliance requirements. Always confirm the exact scope before comparing numbers.

What's usually included

  • Cameras and mounting brackets
  • DVR (analog) or NVR (IP) recorder with a hard drive
  • Cabling, conduit and connectors
  • Power supply and network configuration
  • Mobile app setup for remote viewing

What drives the price up or down

1. Camera type and resolution

Analog HD cameras are cheaper but lower quality. IP cameras give sharper footage, better night vision and features like motion analytics, but they cost more and often need a network switch. Higher resolution (4MP, 8MP) also increases storage requirements, which affects the recorder and hard drive size.

2. Recording and storage

A larger hard drive stores more days of footage before overwriting. Many businesses want 30 days of retention, which pushes storage cost. Some sites also add cloud backup or a second recorder for redundancy.

3. Cabling and site conditions

Long cable runs, ceiling-void work, external routing and drilling through concrete all add labour hours. A retrofit in a finished office costs more than cabling during a fit-out.

4. SIRA compliance (Dubai)

In Dubai, many commercial premises must install a CCTV system that meets Security Industry Regulatory Agency (SIRA) standards, using a SIRA-approved contractor. SIRA-compliant systems have minimum requirements for camera placement, resolution, retention period and recorder security. This raises cost but is mandatory for regulated premises, so confirm whether your business falls under it before accepting a cheaper non-compliant quote. Abu Dhabi and other emirates have their own security authority requirements.

Supply-only vs turnkey

You can buy hardware yourself and hire an installer separately, but a turnkey quote (supply plus install plus configuration plus warranty) is usually cleaner for accountability. If one part fails, you have a single point of responsibility. For SIRA-regulated sites, turnkey through an approved contractor is the safer route.

How to compare CCTV quotes fairly

Cheap headline numbers often hide gaps. Before you accept anything, check that each quote states:

  • Exact camera model, resolution and brand
  • Recorder type, channels and hard drive size (in TB and retention days)
  • Whether SIRA compliance is included (if required)
  • Cabling material and whether conduit is included
  • Warranty period and post-installation support
  • Whether mobile/remote viewing setup is included

Ongoing costs to budget for

  • Maintenance: periodic camera cleaning, firmware updates and checks
  • Hard drive replacement: drives running 24/7 wear out over a few years
  • SIRA renewal: where applicable, systems may need periodic recertification

Getting an accurate quote

FAQ

Do I need SIRA approval for CCTV in Dubai?

Many commercial premises in Dubai must have a SIRA-compliant system installed by a SIRA-approved contractor. Requirements depend on your business type, so confirm your obligation before buying a non-compliant setup that may need replacing.

Is IP CCTV worth the extra cost over analog?

For most businesses that need clear footage for identification, evidence or compliance, IP cameras are worth it thanks to higher resolution and better night performance. For a small basic deterrent, HD analog can be enough.

How much footage should I store?

Thirty days is a common target and is often required for compliance. Longer retention or higher-resolution cameras mean a larger hard drive, so factor storage into the recorder spec when comparing quotes.

how-much-does-epoxy-flooring-cost-in-the.body_html:
Epoxy flooring is one of the most common upgrades for UAE warehouses, workshops, commercial kitchens, car parks and showrooms. It is durable, easy to clean and handles the heat and heavy footfall typical of industrial areas across Dubai, Sharjah and Abu Dhabi. But because "epoxy" covers everything from a thin roller coat to a 3mm self-levelling system, prices swing widely. This 2026 guide breaks down realistic rates and what actually drives the number on your quote.

Epoxy flooring cost per sqm in the UAE (2026)

As an indicative range for supply-and-apply work, expect the following. These are market-observed ranges, not fixed prices, and the final rate depends heavily on area size and floor condition.

  • Standard epoxy coating (2 coats, roller): roughly AED 35-60 per sqm
  • Epoxy with primer + broadcast finish (anti-slip): roughly AED 55-90 per sqm
  • Self-levelling epoxy (1.5-3mm): roughly AED 90-180 per sqm
  • Heavy-duty industrial / PU epoxy: roughly AED 150-280 per sqm
  • Epoxy line marking (car parks / warehouses): roughly AED 8-20 per linear metre

Larger continuous areas (say 1,000 sqm and above) usually attract a lower per-sqm rate because mobilisation and labour are spread across more coverage. Small or awkward areas cost more per sqm.

What is included in a proper epoxy job

  • Surface preparation (grinding or shot blasting)
  • Crack and joint repair, plus moisture check
  • Primer coat
  • Body coat(s) and finish coat
  • Curing time and handover cleaning

What drives the price up or down

1. Surface preparation

This is the biggest hidden cost. Mechanical diamond grinding or shot blasting is essential for adhesion, and if the existing floor is oily, cracked, or has an old coating to remove, prep alone can add AED 15-40 per sqm. A quote that skips proper prep is the most common reason epoxy peels within a year.

2. Thickness and system type

A thin decorative coat for a showroom is a fraction of the cost of a 3mm self-levelling system for a forklift-heavy warehouse. Match the specification to the load, not just the look.

3. Slip resistance and chemical exposure

Commercial kitchens and wet areas often need anti-slip broadcast finishes and food-safe or chemical-resistant systems, which cost more than a plain warehouse coat.

4. Moisture and slab condition

High moisture in the slab requires a moisture-tolerant primer. Skipping this in the UAE's ground-floor slabs is a frequent cause of blistering.

5. Area size and access

Occupied buildings, night-work requirements and multiple small rooms all push the price up compared with one open, empty slab.

Supply-only vs turnkey

If you only need materials, an epoxy kit is far cheaper, but application is where most floors fail. For anything beyond a small storeroom, turnkey (materials plus professional grinding and application with a warranty) is the safer buy. When you request quotes, state clearly whether you want supply-only or turnkey so suppliers price the same scope.

How to compare epoxy flooring quotes fairly

Cheap epoxy quotes usually cut corners on preparation or coat thickness, and the difference only shows up months later. Before you compare numbers, make sure every quote covers the same scope:

  • Preparation method stated (grinding vs shot blasting vs acid etch)
  • System type and total dry film thickness in mm or microns
  • Number of coats and product brand
  • Anti-slip finish included or not
  • Curing / re-use time before you can walk or drive on it
  • Warranty period in writing
  • Site condition assumptions (any repair works excluded?)

A well-structured request gets you comparable numbers instead of a spread you cannot interpret. FAQ

How long does epoxy flooring last in the UAE?

A properly prepared and applied system typically lasts 5-10 years in commercial use, and longer for heavy-duty systems. Poor surface preparation is the main reason floors fail early, so prioritise prep over the cheapest coating price.

Can epoxy be applied over old tiles or existing flooring?

Sometimes, but the surface must be mechanically prepared and sound. Loose tiles, oil contamination or high slab moisture must be resolved first. A good contractor will inspect before quoting rather than promising a coat straight over anything.

How much downtime should I plan for?

Most systems need curing time before foot traffic (often 12-24 hours) and longer before heavy or vehicle loads (typically several days). Ask each supplier to confirm re-use times so you can schedule around your operations.
